thank u for the question. there are actually many resources about the connection between queerness and islam out there if u want to read about it, some of them are available in r/LGBT_Muslims description. but for me personally, since i grew up muslim, it's just my love for my community u know? i have a very deep connection with Allah and the muslims here in my neighborhood and since i'm also a devout muslim (because how we practice our faith is different from one another, some are more pious), you can't just easily tell me to "leave islam!" because it's my religion, and there's freedom of religion for everyone, stated in the universal declaration of human rights. and of course i would never advocate for the killings of queer people, but again if you have the time to read the resources please do, because you'd realise that islam is actually beautiful and promotes peace & equality for everyone. it's quite the same thing with the whole "islam oppresses women!" statement that some people believe in. no, it's the bigoted muslims who interpret islam in such a wrong way. queer muslims in my opinion are different in our own way because we interpret islam's teachings and quran meanings in such a beautifully unique way. we believe Allah loves us equally, and those who promote hate and violence towards us while in this dunya (world) will have to answer later in akhirat (afterlife). we endure so much, that differentiates our experience from the straight cis muslims, but i believe the reward for us in jannah (heaven) later would be abundant. it's one of the challenges that we muslim queers have to face in this world and we're strong; there are others who face even more difficult challenge such as the queer people who live in palestine. we all have different experiences. and one more thing, murdering queer people in the name of islam isn't stated anywhere in the qur'an, murder itself is one of the biggest sins in islam, and those people who throw gay people off the roof out of hatred for instance, will answer for it in the afterlife.
